judgment.rationale: First PO is 'add two whole numbers from 1 to 3 with sum less than 5' (Topic: Addition, Theme: Basic Operations); second PO is 'count correctly up to 5' (Topic: Whole numbers 1-5, Theme: Number and Numeration). Both are PRIMARY ONE Performance Objectives (rank 0). Accurate counting of quantities up to 5 is a foundational numeracy skill that supports success in adding whole numbers whose sum is less than 5, since early addition within this range relies on counting objects/quantities. This supports a developmental direction from the counting objective to the addition objective, beyond the mere shared 'whole numbers' token overlap.

judgment.rationale: Both are Performance Objectives under the same Topic '2. Length' (PRIMARY TWO). The second SFI (Objective 1) has pupils compare their natural units of length (e.g. arm's length) with one another; the first SFI (Objective 4) has pupils identify the need for standardized units of length measurement. Experiencing the variability/limitations of natural-unit comparison substantively supports recognizing why standardized units are needed, a coherent developmental progression, so the natural-units objective builds towards the standardized-units objective. Shared LC tags (length, measurement, units) confirm topical coherence rather than mere lexical overlap; same-rank direction is justified by this pedagogical dependency.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives under the same Addition topic (Theme/Sub-Theme Basic Operations). The first is an awareness/application objective ('mention the need for correct addition of numbers and fractions in everyday activities') while the second is a procedural skill ('add 3-digit numbers'). They share substantive conceptual coherence around addition and reinforce each other, but neither clearly grounds the other's success: appreciating the everyday need for addition does not depend on 3-digit computation, and computing does not depend on the affective/awareness statement. With identical rank (PRIMARY THREE, rank 2) and no substantive evidence establishing a developmental direction, relatesTo is the supported symmetric judgment; shared topic, page proximity, and token/LC overlap alone do not establish a buildsTowards direction.
